representation_notes: Natural l represents the original nonnegative integer λ; l+1 and Fin (l+1) encode n and I. V is an arbitrary complex module with endomorphisms; the Chevalley relations and the generator-invariant-subspace condition encode the given irreducible representation. M is an arbitrary integer submodule, equivalently an additive subgroup, and its basis/admissibility assumptions are not minimal-lattice assumptions. LR.R is the rational subring generated by the prescribed fractions; T004 proves it consists exactly of those fractions. MR is its span in V, not an assumed tensor embedding. J is a comap, exactly the scalars carrying e_i into MR. Tensors put the scalar factor first; their flips give the original ordering. Actions contains actual integer restrictions with agreement equations, not assumed preservation. induced is Mathlib baseChange. Output predicates only package explicit statements; none supplies a proof. Matrix units are coordinate maps of an actual supplied basis. Quotients and all transport maps will be checked in local obligations.

steps.statement: LR.Strings l x y h v
steps.explanation: Induct using the commutators; iterate x on y^i v and use positive nonzero characteristic-zero factors to prove every e_i nonzero.

steps.statement: LR.CBasis l y v
steps.explanation: Isolate coefficients with the polynomial in h, obtain independence, use dimension for spanning, then compare coefficients at eigenvalue -l-2 to terminate the string.

steps.statement: LR.N1 l x y h v
steps.explanation: Divide by factorials for the elementary matrices; iterate them, including zero boundaries. Use the falling-product/factorial identity for Nat.choose, so the coefficients are integral.

steps.statement: (∀ q : ℚ, q ∈ LR.localRing p ↔ ∃ a d : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d ∧ q = (a : ℚ)/d) ∧ LR.LocalBasis p l M
steps.explanation: Check the fractions are a subring (primality controls denominator products), identifying the closure encoding with R. Compare the shared integer/complex basis with N001, reindex by Fin(l+1), base-change and prove the multiplication map is injective and onto MR.

steps.statement: LR.LocalStable p M x y
steps.explanation: Extend divided-power preservation from M to its R-span by complex linearity.

steps.statement: ∀ b : Module.Basis (Fin (l+1)) ℂ V, (∀ i, b i = LR.vec y v i.val) → LR.PartialUnits l x y b
steps.explanation: Test the three partial matrix-unit identities on each e_k, using the full divided-power formulas and both zero ranges.

steps.statement: LR.N2 p l M x y v
steps.explanation: Factorials below p are units in R, so choose(l,j) is a unit. Compose the partial identities, invert the scalar, and deduce all matrix units preserve MR. Package the scalar-extension basis and span statements.

steps.statement: LR.Decomposition p l M y v
steps.explanation: Projections E_ii identify their images with J_i e_i, and E_ij makes all J_i equal. Sum projections for the direct decomposition; project a finite basis to prove finite generation and use complex spanning for nonzeroness.

steps.statement: LR.TensorLine p M y v
steps.explanation: Construct multiplication on Q⊗R J. Verify Q localizes R at nonzero elements, reduce each tensor to a single fraction, and prove injectivity and the rational-span image. Base-change a finite generating list.

steps.statement: Nonempty (TensorProduct (LR.R p) ℚ (LR.MR p M) ≃ₗ[ℚ] (Fin (l+1) → TensorProduct (LR.R p) ℚ (LR.J p M y v 0))) ∧ LR.RankOne p M y v
steps.explanation: Tensor the direct decomposition using its coordinate maps, checking the balanced maps are inverse. Compare dimension l+1 from the local basis with (l+1) times the finite rational dimension of T; cancel l+1>0.

steps.statement: LR.Generators p M y v
steps.explanation: Choose a nonzero a and finite nonzero generating list. Injectivity of multiplication makes 1⊗a nonzero; rank one makes it span, yielding nonzero rational multiples of a.

steps.statement: LR.Valuations p M y v
steps.explanation: For each nonzero rational generator, repeatedly divide numerator and denominator by p, terminating by descent on positive integers. Their remaining ratio is a unit of R; subtract the exponents.

steps.statement: LR.N3 p l M y v
steps.explanation: Take the minimum of finitely many exponents and put b=p^nu a. All generators lie in Rb, and a minimal one gives b in J. For every nonzero generator b, spanning follows from the direct decomposition and independence from N001. Package multiplication injectivity and rank one.

steps.statement: ∃ (c : CharP K p) (rho : LR.R p →+* K) (sigma : LR.R p →+* ZMod p) (A : LR.Actions M x y h), LR.ResidueMaps K p c rho sigma
steps.explanation: Use characteristic p to show all permitted integer denominators survive; define rho and sigma by fractions and verify their kernels and the quotient isomorphism. Build integer restrictions of x,y and all divided powers; h=xy-yx preserves M as well.

steps.statement: ∀ (c : CharP K p) (rho : LR.R p →+* K) (sigma : LR.R p →+* ZMod p), LR.ResidueMaps K p c rho sigma → LR.Transport K p M c rho sigma
steps.explanation: Construct the F_p-module structure on MR/pMR through the residue quotient. Build both scalar-extension equivalences and their inverses on pure tensors; check balancing and intertwining of every compatible induced operator.

steps.statement: ∀ (c : CharP K p) (rho : LR.R p →+* K) (sigma : LR.R p →+* ZMod p) (A : LR.Actions M x y h), LR.ResidueMaps K p c rho sigma → LR.Reduction K p l M x y h v A c rho sigma
steps.explanation: For every generating scalar b and every corresponding R-basis, base-change it and transport to VK. Reduce its coordinates to construct the F_p-basis of MR/pMR. On pure tensors obtain the generator formulas and the transport of every restricted complex matrix unit.

steps.statement: LR.N4 K p l M x y h v
steps.explanation: For r≤l<p, r! remains nonzero. Transport r! X_r=x^r and the y identity from M, then reduce the matrix-unit factorization. For every basis with the indicated generator matrices the same formula holds; invariance under powers, scalars and compositions proves invariance under all units.

steps.statement: ∃ (A : LR.Actions M x y h) (beta : Module.Basis (Fin (l+1)) K (LR.VK K M)), Nontrivial (LR.VK K M) ∧ ∀ W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M), LR.inv W (LR.induced K M A.lx.map) → LR.inv W (LR.induced K M A.ly.map) → ∀ i j, LR.inv W (LR.unit l beta i j)
steps.explanation: Choose an allowed generating scalar and its transported basis. beta_0 is nonzero because Fin(l+1) is nonempty; extract the universal matrix-unit invariance.

steps.statement: ∀ (beta : Module.Basis (Fin (l+1)) K (LR.VK K M)) (W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M)), (∀ i j, LR.inv W (LR.unit l beta i j)) → W ≠ ⊥ → W = ⊤
steps.explanation: In the nonzero subspace choose w and a nonzero coordinate jointly. E_ij w equals that coordinate times beta_i, so division puts every beta_i in W and spanning gives W=top.

steps.statement: ∃ A : LR.Actions M x y h, Nontrivial (LR.VK K M) ∧ ∀ W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M), LR.inv W (LR.induced K M A.lx.map) → LR.inv W (LR.induced K M A.ly.map) → LR.inv W (LR.induced K M A.lh.map) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
steps.explanation: For arbitrary W invariant under the generators, split W=0 or not, and apply the matrix-unit lemma in the nonzero branch. Discharge invariance hypotheses. Generator-span invariance is precisely the original Chevalley L(K)-module formulation, including characteristic two.
